name: Jason Wei
headline: Battery Engineering at Tesla, in Palo Alto.
summary: Mechanical Design Engineer in Battery Engineering at Tesla, in Palo Alto. I studied mechanical engineering at UCSB, was on Gaucho Racing’s FSAE Electric team, and still like cars, Miatas, track driving, and building web apps.
bio: I’ve been into cars for about as long as I could read. Supercar picture books, license plates on the road, quizzing my grandma on whatever drove by. I studied mechanical engineering at UCSB.
At school I was on Gaucho Racing, the Formula SAE Electric team, as Chief Electrical Engineer. We designed, built, and raced an electric car.
These days I’m a Mechanical Design Engineer in Battery Engineering at Tesla in Palo Alto. Off the clock it’s still cars — Miatas especially — plus track driving and building web apps.
tagline: Cars, Miatas, track days, and web apps.

bullets: Owned the design and DFM of two new die-cast high-voltage connector headers.
Designed a new face seal profile, iterated with Ansys hyperelastic simulations, improving the contact pressure to reaction force ratio by 52% over existing designs.
Designed critical-fastening snap joints, parametrically optimized for low insertion force and high retention force by linking CAD dimensions as Ansys input parameters across the design space.

Evaluated face seal performance boundaries under worst-case top cover deflections across thicknesses, materials, and stamping geometries, cutting header per-unit cost by 10% after removing unnecessary fasteners.
Routed harnesses and busbars in CAD to reduce bends and installation-order constraints.
Owned design and manufacturing of 8 wire-bonded and potted 2170 battery modules forming a 538 V, 6.2 kWh, 81.9 kW pack.
Designed external HV distribution and internal ancillaries (main contactors, mid-pack main fuse, HV disconnect, battery maintenance plugs).
Designed battery water-cooling cold plates, flow-simulated in SolidWorks Flow and validated the pressure-drop curve on a test rig.
Built MATLAB thermal models for cell-level fusible link sizing and pack-level thermal limits.
Designed and implemented heat sinking solutions for thermal camera microprocessor; simulated in Solidworks Thermal study and validated in environmental chamber.
Machined go-no-go gauges for quantifying thermal shrinkage defects in injection molded PPSU plastic.
Created Excel script for analyzing worst-case and statistical tolerance stack-ups.
Created 30+ Agile ECOs and GD&T drawings for new products and product revisions.
Designed and manufactured 3 blackbodies with operating temperatures from −40°C to 60°C for infrared sensor calibration.
Instructed over 200 researchers and grad students in workshop and microfluidic equipment.
Fabricated and delivered over 100 CNC milled, 3D printed, and laser cut custom user orders.
Managed, repaired, and created SOPs for 3D printers and laser cutters (Formlabs Form 3, Ultimaker S5, Stratasys F270, Stratasys Objet 30 Pro, and Rayjet 300).
CNC milled and 3D printed a fluid boiling fixture for a NASA ISS experiment, analyzing the role of surface structures on flow boiling instabilities.
Researched and presented the use of vapor chambers, which utilize liquid-gas phase change, as a heat spreader for EV battery thermal management.
Characterizing heat pipe thermal gradients and thermal conductivities using custom built test bench.
Presented research on a novel EV battery cooling method at the UCSB CSEP Colloquium Poster Session in August 2023.
